lead_with.title: The binder inside the mast-cell CAR
lead_with.text: Their whole platform depends on a **mast-cell-selective scFv**. MAbSilico designs **epitope-specific, humanized, high-affinity** binders against any target in **~21 days** — offer to design or optimize the targeting domain (selectivity vs other FcεRI/KIT-expressing cells is the hard part).

lead_with.title: Speak her language: validation
lead_with.text: She will ask how predictions are checked. Recap MAbSilico's wet-lab loop: binding by **cytometry, BLI, HTRF**; developability with partner **Sartorius**. Bring one predicted-vs-measured example.

lead_with.title: Fewer wet-lab rounds before animal work
lead_with.text: For an angel-stage company, every design cycle burns runway. In silico screening of many binder variants before mRNA-LNP work in vivo = **less cost, faster go/no-go** for the next raise.

person.name: Ramya Yarlagadda
person.text: Senior protein engineer, **15 years** in industry. Joined AllerGene **Aug 2026**. Before: **EXUMA Biotechnology** (2020–2024: paramyxovirus envelopes for **in vivo CAR-T** delivery, TNFα kill switch, solid-tumor CARs), **Precigen** (2016–2020: antibody epitope engineering, **in silico humanization**, CAR-T designs, EGFR kill-switch patent, IL-12 patent), **Intrexon** (2010–2016: scFv, scFab, BiTEs, DARPins). Since 2024 also independent consultant (**VyteK**) on AI-driven protein engineering. Reviewer for *Antibodies* and *Frontiers in Immunology*. University of the Sciences in Philadelphia. Based in Greater Phoenix.

company.text: AllerGene AI Therapeutics (Miami, founded 2025) engineers CAR-T cells **directly inside the body** with mRNA delivered by T-cell-targeted lipid nanoparticles. The CAR-T cells are transient and repeatable and target **tissue-resident mast cells**, the cells that trigger severe allergic reactions — the goal is to reset the allergic response rather than suppress symptoms. CEO Sid Kerkar presented the platform at Hanson Wade's **In Vivo Cell Engineering & Gene Editing Summit** (Boston, Jul 30, 2026). Target indications: severe food allergy, anaphylaxis, chronic urticaria, mast cell diseases.

financials.text: Private, **angel stage** (CB Insights). No public revenue or funding amount found. Small team: CEO, executive manager (Ashley Oxley), senior scientist (Ramya). Budget is tight — a **paid pilot on one binder** is a more realistic first step than a platform deal.

industry.title: In vivo CAR-T is the hot cell-therapy trend
industry.text: mRNA-LNP in vivo CAR-T avoids cell manufacturing; many 2026 deals in oncology and autoimmunity. Allergy is a new, less crowded indication.

industry.title: Selectivity is the risk
industry.text: Mast-cell markers are shared with other cells (basophils, stem cells for KIT). Binder specificity is the key safety question — exactly where epitope-specific design helps.

talking_points: Did the one-pager answer your questions? What would you want to see in a technical deep-dive?
Which **mast-cell antigen** does your CAR target today, and where does the current scFv come from (in-house, licensed, library)?
What limits it most: **selectivity** vs basophils/other cells, **affinity**, or expression/stability in the CAR format?
How do you validate binders today — would our **cytometry / BLI / HTRF** readouts plug into your assays?
Would a **paid pilot on one binder** (~21 days to candidates) help your next go/no-go or financing round?
Who signs off on external partners — Sid directly? Should he join the next call?
